chain.title: Splitting the Grain
chain.desc: One gunpowder shaken apart into pinches, and nine pinches pressed back into one. The mod's smallest unit of propellant and the start of every charge.

chain.title: A Cannon Made of Tree
chain.desc: Logs packed around gunpowder. Weak, short-lived and liable to burst, but it fires today rather than after a foundry.

chain.title: Bolting It Together
chain.desc: Andesite casing, a piston extension pole, iron plates and nuggets. Right-click a stack of cannon blocks and it welds them into one working gun.

chain.title: Shoving It Home
chain.desc: A piston extension pole through planks. Mounted on a contraption or hafted onto a stick, it drives shot and charge down to the breech.

chain.title: The Cloth Bag
chain.desc: String and wool. Cannons do not take loose powder; propellant travels in sewn bags, and this is the bag before it is filled.

chain.title: Measured Fury
chain.desc: An empty charge stuffed with packed gunpowder, itself compacted from loose grain. Stack charges behind a shot to trade barrel life for range.

chain.title: Iron Beats Timber
chain.desc: Iron plates hammered around gunpowder. The first metal cannon block, holding far more pressure than any log ever will.

chain.title: Capping the Muzzle
chain.desc: Iron plates, an iron ingot and gunpowder. Seals the far end of a barrel so the pressure has only one way out, and only one direction to throw.

chain.title: Pointed and Left There
chain.desc: Andesite casing, iron plates and gunpowder. Holds a cannon rigidly on one bearing so it can be fired by redstone but never aimed.

chain.title: Traverse and Elevate
chain.desc: Andesite casing, a shaft, iron plates and gunpowder. Takes rotation on two axes so a controller or a rider can swing the gun onto a target.

chain.title: Dragging the Gun
chain.desc: A shaft, planks and a pair of cannon wheels cut from logs and iron plate. Turns a static emplacement into something a horse or a player can move.

chain.title: Iron and Charcoal
chain.desc: Iron compacted with coal in a basin. Brittle under repeated fire but cheap, and the only metal you can pour before the foundry gets serious.

chain.title: Sand That Remembers
chain.desc: Clay, dirt and sand mixed by hand. Packed under a mould it holds the shape while molten metal is poured on top of it.

chain.title: Turning a Basin into a Foundry
chain.desc: Plain andesite alloy. Set it over a heated Create basin and the basin will melt ingots into molten metal instead of mixing them.

chain.title: The Shape of a Bore
chain.desc: A log cut on a mechanical saw. Stack moulds on casting sand, pour molten metal in and the cast hardens into an unbored cannon block.

chain.title: Solid Through
chain.desc: Molten cast iron poured into a very small mould. It looks like a barrel but there is no hole in it yet, so it will not chamber anything.

chain.title: Cutting the Hole
chain.desc: Andesite casing, a fluid pipe, a piston extension pole and iron. Driven along a contraption it bores solid castings out into working barrels.

chain.title: It Has a Throat Now
chain.desc: The unbored casting after the drill has passed through it. Stack these end to end and every extra block adds range and muzzle velocity.

chain.title: The Wedge
chain.desc: A cogwheel and cast iron. Slides across the back of a breech to seal it, letting the gun be loaded from behind instead of down the muzzle.

chain.title: Faster Than the Ramrod
chain.desc: A cogwheel, a large cogwheel and a lever. Converts a sliding breech into a quick-firing one that cycles on rotation instead of on patience.

chain.title: Nobody Rams By Hand
chain.desc: Andesite casing, a piston extension pole and gunpowder. Feeds charge and shell into a breech automatically so the gun keeps its rhythm.

chain.title: The Better Alloy
chain.desc: Iron mixed with coal in a heated basin. Steel holds pressures that split cast iron, and it is the first metal worth building a big gun from.

chain.title: Shrinking Steel On
chain.desc: A blaze burner, a valve handle and brass and iron plates. Heats stacked cannon layers until they fuse into a single built-up barrel.

chain.title: It Goes Off On Arrival
chain.desc: Mechanical crafting from iron, wooden slabs and high explosive filler. Fitted with a fuze it detonates on contact instead of merely punching through.

notes: Create: Big Cannons assumes base Create is finished. Derived base-Create dependencies: create:andesite_alloy, create:andesite_casing, create:shaft, create:cogwheel, create:large_cogwheel, create:piston_extension_pole, create:fluid_pipe, create:precision_mechanism, create:blaze_burner and create:valve_handles, plus a heated Create basin (for melting and for the steel/bronze alloy mixes), a mechanical saw (all eight cast moulds are create:cutting from logs), a mechanical press for forge:plates/iron and forge:plates/brass, and Create sequenced assembly for the recoil spring, the autocannon cartridge and the autocannon breech extractors. CRITICAL SOURCING NOTE: 100 of the 194 valid ids have no recipe file under data/createbigcannons/recipes/**. They are NOT unobtainable - they come from a second registry, data/createbigcannons/block_recipes/** (69 files), which this research parsed separately: 30 createbigcannons:cannon_casting entries (molten metal poured into a cast_shape on casting sand -> unbored_* block), 28 createbigcannons:drill_boring entries (unbored_* + cannon drill -> bored block), and 10 createbigcannons:built_up_heating entries (stacked *_cannon_layer blocks + cannon welder -> built_up_* barrel). Every wheel-2 barrel and chamber id was verified against those three registries, not guessed. Chain ordering follows cast_iron (compacting iron+coal) -> bronze (mixing copper+zinc+cinder flour, or copper+tin) -> steel (mixing iron+coal) -> nethersteel (mixing steel or cast iron + netherite scrap), which is the melting/alloy graph exactly. ORDERING CONFLICT vs moddb consensus (22 entries, ALL 22 id-verified, none renamed or impossible): the consensus is mould-saturated - 8 of its 22 entries are cast moulds (small 0.281, screw_breech 0.384, autocannon_recoil_spring 0.410, medium 0.468, cannon_end 0.521, autocannon_breech 0.570, autocannon_barrel 0.604, sliding_breech 0.688, very_large 0.708, very_small 0.747, large 0.748), spread across the whole book as if each were a separate progression beat. They are not: all eight are one create:cutting recipe from a log, differing only in cast_shape, so they were collapsed into a single wheel behind small_cast_mould. This is exactly the wheel-not-chain case the brief calls out. Second conflict: consensus contains no cannon barrel, no chamber, no breech, no ingot and no shell - the entire casting and boring payoff of the mod is absent from it, presumably because those items are produced by block_recipes rather than by JSON crafting recipes and so are invisible to recipe-graph scrapers. The recipe graph was preferred and the barrel/chamber/breech line put on the spine. Consensus positions that survive: cannon_builder 0.234, ram_head 0.272, casting_sand 0.414, cannon_drill 0.491, cannon_mount 0.627, fixed_cannon_mount 0.819 - all consistent with the recipe graph and kept near those points. DROPPED - valid ids with no obtainment route in any of the four registries: createbigcannons:traffic_cone (a projectile block with a munition_properties entry and a loot table but no recipe anywhere), createbigcannons:yaw_controller (cannon mount part, no recipe), createbigcannons:cannon_crafting_wand and createbigcannons:creative_autocannon_ammo_container (creative-only). Intermediates deliberately excluded from the spine because they are transitional items inside a sequenced assembly or a boring step and would read as busywork: all 11 incomplete_*, all 4 partial_*/partially_* and all 21 unbored_* ids except unbored_cast_iron_cannon_barrel, which is kept as one step precisely to teach the cast-then-bore loop. createbigcannons:molten_*_bucket ids are valid but are fluid containers with no recipe file. Nuggets and scrap (cast_iron_nugget, bronze_scrap, steel_scrap, nethersteel_nugget) excluded per desirability - authors quest the ingot, never the nugget. Also valid and craftable but cut for length: worm, worm_head, ram_rod, mortar_stone, wrought_iron_drop_mortar_end, log_cannon_end, pair_of_cannon_wheels, packed_gunpowder, packed_guncotton, guncotton, nitropowder, congealed_nitro, hardened_nitro, gas_mask, block_armor_inspection_tool, machine_gun_round, big_cartridge, filled_autocannon_cartridge, autocannon_ammo_container, tracer_tip, delayed_impact_fuze, delayed_inertia_fuze, and the bronze/steel/nethersteel ingot and block ids.
